justifications.c1: Only an old industry aggregate (200,000 cylinders/£9m, c.2012, search-confirmed) and per-incident losses described as 'hundreds of pounds' (Ryde, 14 cylinders); no per-stockist or per-incident £ figure ≥£2k.
justifications.c2: Many local overnight cage thefts reported (Prees, Braunston, Kingsbury, Wrexham, Oxford, Diss) but no national or per-stockist rate; run-empty-between-restocks frequency not evidenced at all.
justifications.c3: Locked cages exist and are defeated by cutting; the researcher found no source for manual cage counts by drivers or their labour cost.
justifications.c4: Codes (Liquid Gas UK CoP 7, Flogas code, Jersey standard) cover safe storage only; researcher states none require monitoring, stock or theft records; HSE ATEX page adds a constraint rather than pressure.
justifications.c5: Calor 'Sales Professional' roles (£48k-£57.6k) cover the cylinder network, but no evidence anyone at Calor/Flogas holds budget for cage security or telemetry; a sale to a single large gas company is an enterprise sale.
justifications.c6: Calor (300+ retailers) and Flogas account managers/distributors visit cages, but no evidence they sell or bundle any technology to stockists.
justifications.c7: Otodata cage monitor (search-confirmed) proves the restock use case in North America at low fees ($1-$5/month); no UK product found but the gap is asserted, and pricing expectations are low.
justifications.c8: Door/tamper sensing is easy, but cylinder counting needs load cells or a custom circuit; electronics at an LPG cage raise DSEAR/ATEX questions; no BOM found.
justifications.c9: Comparable monitors priced at $1-$5/month per unit; no insurer, police or compliance demand for ongoing cage data found.
justifications.c10: Local news (many), Gasworld trade press, a Caravan Club forum thread (personal theft, tangential) and an Irish court case; no regulator or insurer loss data.

weakest: Per-site losses are a few hundred pounds per theft and the only large figure is a decade-old industry aggregate, while the comparable product sells for $1-$5 per month.
